record.original_question: A semi-dispersive billiard table is one whose boundary has dispersive inward-convex components together with neutral components such as line segments. Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A planar billiard table is a compact, connected region $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial Y$, on which the billiard flow is defined by free motion in the interior together with elastic reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at smooth points of the boundary. A boundary component is called dispersive if it is smooth and strictly convex when viewed from the inside of $Y$ (so that it scatters parallel beams of trajectories), and neutral if it is a straight line segment. Call $Y$ a semi-dispersive billiard table if every smooth component of $\partial Y$ is either dispersive or neutral, and at least one component is dispersive.

The billiard flow is called hyperbolic if it has nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere with respect to the natural invariant (Liouville) measure on the unit tangent bundle restricted to $Y$.

Question: Is every semi-dispersive billiard table (in the above sense) hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search returned the original problem listing and general literature on semi-dispersing billiards (hard ball systems, Boltzmann–Sinai hypothesis, transversal fundamental theorem). No source was found that explicitly resolves the question of whether every planar semi-dispersive billiard table (dispersive arcs plus neutral line-segment components) is hyperbolic. The status therefore appears unverified from available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey on hyperbolicity and ergodicity of semi-dispersing billiards including hard ball systems.
status_evidence.claim: General hyperbolicity results exist for specific semi-dispersing classes but no universal answer for the planar setting described.

status_evidence.title: A Transversal Fundamental Theorem for semi-dispersing billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Tools to prove ergodicity and K-property of semidispersing billiards under transversality assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity/ergodicity proofs require additional hypotheses, suggesting the general planar question remains nontrivial.
